rubric.why: Density is defined as mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that density is mass per unit volume.

rubric.why: Elasticity describes a body's return to its original form after the deforming force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body regains its original shape or size when the deforming force is removed.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Elasticity is the property of a body by which it regains its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The graph must identify the velocities and the time interval used in the derivation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for representing initial velocity u, final velocity v and time t on the velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using the slope of the graph as acceleration.

rubric.why: This is the acceleration relation obtained from the graph.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly writing the relation between a, u, v and t.

rubric.why: This is the first equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the first equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for obtaining v = u + at.

modelAnswer: On a velocity-time graph, let the velocity change from u to v in time t.
The slope of the graph is acceleration, a = (v - u)/t.
Therefore, at = v - u.
Hence, v = u + at, the first equation of motion.

items.followUp: State and explain the two conditions for rotational equilibrium.

rubric.why: Zero resultant force is the condition for translational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the first condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that the resultant force on the body is zero.

rubric.why: With zero resultant force, the body has no linear acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the body remains at rest or moves with uniform velocity.

rubric.why: Zero resultant torque is the condition for rotational equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the second condition for equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant torque about any point is zero.

modelAnswer: A body is in equilibrium when it has no linear or angular acceleration.
First condition: the resultant force acting on the body must be zero, ΣF = 0.
Then the body remains at rest or moves with uniform velocity.
Second condition: the resultant torque acting on the body must be zero, Στ = 0.

items.followUp: A car travels at a steady speed of 10 m s^-1 against a resistance of 600 N. Calculate the power of its engine.

rubric.why: At steady speed, the engine's driving force balances the water resistance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for equating the engine force to the 4000 N resistance.

rubric.why: Power is the product of force and speed.
rubric.description: Uses the power relation and substitutes the values.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for using P = Fv and substituting 4000 N and 4 m s^-1.

rubric.why: The calculated power is 16000 W.
rubric.description: Gives the answer with a suitable unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct power and unit.

modelAnswer: Given: speed, v = 4 m s^-1; water resistance, F = 4000 N.
Since the boat moves at steady speed, the engine force balances the water resistance: F = 4000 N.
Power, P = Fv.
The power of the engine is 16000 W (16 kW).

items.followUp: An object weighs 25 N in air and 15 N in water. Calculate its density and suggest a possible material.

rubric.why: The loss of weight in water is the upthrust, equal to 6.6 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for calculating 18 N - 11.4 N = 6.6 N.

rubric.why: Relative density equals weight in air divided by loss of weight in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for calculating the ratio 18/6.6, approximately 2.73.

rubric.why: Multiplying relative density by water's density gives an object density of about 2.7 × 10^3 kg m^-3.
rubric.description: Calculates density with a correct unit.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct density and unit; award 1 mark for a correct numerical value without a unit.

rubric.why: A density close to 2.7 g cm^-3 is characteristic of aluminium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying aluminium (aluminum) as a likely material.

modelAnswer: Given: weight in air = 18 N; weight in water = 11.4 N; density of water = 1000 kg m^-3.
Loss of weight in water = 18 N - 11.4 N = 6.6 N.
Relative density = weight in air / loss of weight in water = 18 N / 6.6 N = 2.73.
Density of object = relative density × density of water.
Density of object = 2.73 × 1000 kg m^-3 = 2727 kg m^-3 ≈ 2.7 × 10^3 kg m^-3.
This density is close to that of aluminium, so the object may be made of aluminium.

items.followUp: Define chemistry and astronomy as branches of physical sciences.

rubric.why: Physical sciences deal with non-living matter and the physical world.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that physical sciences study non-living things or the physical world.

rubric.why: Biological sciences deal with living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that biological sciences study living organisms.

modelAnswer: Physical sciences are the sciences that study non-living things and the physical world.
Biological sciences are the sciences that study living organisms.

items.followUp: What is meant by a derived quantity? Give two examples.

rubric.why: A physical quantity is a measurable property that can be expressed with a magnitude and unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that physical quantities are measurable properties expressed by magnitude and unit.

rubric.why: The answer must provide examples of physical quantities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving any two valid examples, such as length and mass.

modelAnswer: Physical quantities are measurable properties of a body or phenomenon that can be expressed by a magnitude and a unit.
Examples include length and mass.

items.followUp: Define acceleration and write its S.I. unit.

rubric.why: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that velocity is displacement per unit time or the rate of change of displacement.

rubric.why: The S.I. unit of velocity is metre per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing m s^-1 or metre per second.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
Its S.I. unit is metre per second (m s^-1).
